{{nihongo|'''Matsusaka Shrine'''|松阪神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ise Province]].

=== Enshrined deities ===
Its principal deities are {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997|lt=Homutawake-no-Mikoto}} ({{ill|Hachiman|Q261637|qid=Q261637}}) and {{ill|Ukanomitama|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama-no-Kami}} ({{ill|Inari Ōkami|Q719665|qid=Q719665}}). === History ===
It is regarded as a successor shrine of "Oi Shrine" in Iitaka District, Ise Province, listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} (another candidate shrine is {{ill|Kanbe Kotachi Shinmeisha|Q11590193|qid=Q11590193}} in Shimomura-cho, Matsusaka).

Its founding date is unknown, but it has stood on this site since ancient times and was revered by the Iitaka clan, district governors, as their {{ill|Ubusunagami|Q1392097|qid=Q1392097}}.

In {{ill|1588|Q6757|qid=Q6757}} ({{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 16), {{ill|Gamō Ujisato|Q906580|qid=Q906580}} built {{ill|Matsusaka Castle|Q1010226|qid=Q1010226}} in this shrine forest (Oi no Mori), made the shrine the castle guardian, and enshrined the Hachiman deity together with it. From then through the Edo period it was called "Ojohachiman" (Castle Hachiman). In the first year of {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}}, when Yoshida Shigekatsu repaired Matsusaka Castle, Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto was additionally enshrined.

In the early Meiji period, it was identified with the Shikinaisha Oi Shrine and renamed from Ojohachiman to Oi Shrine, then ranked as a gosha in July {{ill|Meiji – year 4|Q11512280|qid=Q11512280}}. On {{ill|March 23|Q2445|qid=Q2445}}, {{ill|1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056}} (Meiji 41), deities from 17 nearby shrines (33 deities in total) were merged and it was renamed Matsusaka Shrine.

=== Festivals ===
In mid-July, this shrine, Hino-cho Yakumo Shrine, and Honmachi Mikuriya Shrine hold a {{ill|Gion Matsuri|Q979873|qid=Q979873}}. Originally this was the festival of Uomachi Uryu Shrine and Nishimachi Yaegaki Shrine, both later merged into this shrine. These shrines were called the "Four Heavenly Kings" as shrines enshrining Matsusaka's {{ill|Gozu Tennō|Q11570247|qid=Q11570247}}.

=== Regular 20-year transfer ===
A {{ill|Sengū|Q2271023|qid=Q2271023|lt=shikinen senza}} is held every 20 years<ref name="ym1609">{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.yukanmie.com/news/1544/|title=Final rite "Oshiraishi Arai" held at Matsusaka Shrine; parishioners prepare for once-every-20-years shikinen sengu next month on the 15th|publisher={{ill|Yukan Mie|Q11430176|qid=Q11430176}}|date=2016-09-12|accessdate=2016-10-10|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20161010144610/http://www.yukanmie.com/news/1544/|archivedate=2016-10-10|url-status=dead|url-status-date=2017-10}}</ref>. In {{ill|2016|Q25245|qid=Q25245}} (Heisei 28), {{ill|Oshiraishimochi|Q17225061|qid=Q17225061|lt=Oshiraishi Arai}} was held on {{ill|September 11|Q2851|qid=Q2851}}, and the transfer took place on {{ill|October 15|Q2919|qid=Q2919}}<ref name="ym1609"/>.
